title: The memorial page she already wrote, without writing it twice
promise: Everything Marion put in her plan — her life story, her photographs, her song — becomes a published memorial page anyone can open, and nothing lands on it that she did not accept.

scenes.title: The page starts from what she already wrote
scenes.proves: Creating your own memorial page while alive, seeded from the plan you have been keeping — name, dates, life story, photos and song, already there.
scenes.watch: Nothing is typed into the page here. The plan is what fills it.

scenes.title: A design that looks like a person, not a form
scenes.proves: Dozens of memorial designs, and the details the page carries: her name, her dates, and a headline in her own words.
scenes.watch: The name and the dates were never typed — they came from the plan.

scenes.title: Everything she wrote is already on the page
scenes.proves: Life story, Memorial page photos and the Memorial page song arrive from the plan's own sections, with no second round of writing or uploading.
scenes.watch: Photos and songs only cross over from the Memorial page group of the plan.

scenes.title: One link, and no account to open it
scenes.proves: Publishing mints a public address that renders the chosen design with the life story, her photograph and the song, open to anyone holding the link.
scenes.watch: The address is minted from her name on the first publish, not chosen by hand.

scenes.title: A neighbour writes to her, with no account
scenes.proves: Anyone holding the link can leave a tribute without signing up for anything.
scenes.watch: No signup, no password, no app — a name, a message, and that is all.

scenes.title: Nothing reaches her page until she accepts it
scenes.proves: Tributes are held for review: approval is the permission that publishes them, and the public page shows nothing before it is given.
scenes.watch: The same tribute, absent a moment ago, appears only after approval.
